claims.claim: **A careful history and a thorough head-to-toe examination** are needed — the range of causes is wide. **Take parents' concerns about behaviour change seriously.**
claims.source_text: A careful history and thorough ‘head to toe’ examination is required to assess for the wide range of causes … Pay particular attention to the concerns of parents about behavioural change
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unexpected changes in physical, social or cognitive abilities can be due to untreated pain.**
claims.source_text: Unexpected changes to children’s physical, social and cognitive abilities can be due to untreated pain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give analgesia while assessing, but be cautious with opioids.** Admission may be needed for observation or investigation.
claims.source_text: Provide analgesia while assessing the child but be cautious with opioid prescription … Admission may be required for observation and/or further investigations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infection:** respiratory, throat, ear, **dental**, urinary, skin/bone/joint, and **meningitis or an infected VP shunt**.
claims.source_text: Infection Upper or lower respiratory tract infection with increased secretions Pharyngitis/tonsillitis with throat pain/reduced intake Otitis media Dental infection UTI Skin, bone, or joint infections Meningitis/infected VP shunt
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Musculoskeletal:** accidental and pathological fractures · **consider non-accidental injury (under-reported in this group)** · hip dislocation or subluxation · contractures · spasticity · back pain and scoliosis.
claims.source_text: Musculoskeletal Accidental fractures Consider non-accidental injury (under reported in this group) Pathological fractures/osteoporosis Hip dislocation or subluxation Contractures Spasticity (can cause pain or is often secondary to pain) Back pain/scoliosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Neurological:** more seizures · dystonia · headache · **raised intracranial pressure — a blocked VP shunt, especially with vomiting or altered consciousness** · neuropathic pain.
claims.source_text: Neurological Increased seizure activity Dystonia Headache Increased intracranial pressure (consider in children with VP shunts - blocked shunt especially with vomiting or change in level of consciousness) Neuropathic pain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal/genitourinary:** constipation · reflux · gallstones · pancreatitis · dysmotility or dumping · feeding-tube problems · renal stones (more likely on topiramate) · dysmenorrhoea · appendicitis · ovarian or testicular torsion.
claims.source_text: Abdominal/genitourinary Constipation Gastro-oesophageal reflux Gallstones Pancreatitis … Issue with feeding tube (if NG/NJ or PEG/PEJ in situ) Renal stones (increased risk if on topiramate) Gynaecological eg dysmenorrhoea Appendicitis Ovarian or testicular torsion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dumping syndrome:** look for post-prandial hypoglycaemia, and evaluate gastric emptying if a PEG/PEJ is in situ.
claims.source_text: Gastro-intestinal motility disorders/dumping syndrome (look for post prandial hypoglycaemia, evaluate gastric emptying if PEG/PEJ in situ)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Psychological and other:** emotional or behavioural difficulty (including changes at home or school), anxiety, depression, ASD/ADHD; sleep deprivation, medications, nutritional deficiency.
claims.source_text: Psychological Emotional and behavioural difficulties (consider changes in environment eg home, school or family) Anxiety or depression ASD or ADHD Other Sleep deprivation (associated with pain and spasm) Medications Nutritional deficiencies
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Establish a timeline** of when the change in behaviour, irritability or pain began.
claims.source_text: Establish a timeline as to when change in behaviour, features of irritability or pain started
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine fully — dentition, ENT, abdomen, hips and limbs** — check blood pressure and any VP shunt, and **dip the urine** for blood (stones) or white cells (infection).
claims.source_text: Full physical examination including dentition, ENT, abdomen, hips and limbs in particular and investigate as indicated Check blood pressure Assess VP shunt if present Check urine for blood (stones) or white cells (infection)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider imaging** (hip X-ray, abdominal US, CT, bone scan, gastroscopy, CT brain) **and a dental review.**
claims.source_text: Consider further imaging that might be useful eg hip X-ray, abdominal US, CT, bone scan, gastroscopy, CT brain Consider dental review
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat identifiable causes and give adequate analgesia.**
claims.source_text: Treat identifiable causes Provide adequate analgesia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Caution with opioids — increased risk of respiratory depression in CP. Seek specialist advice early.**
claims.source_text: Caution with opioid use in children with cerebral palsy due to increased risk of respiratory depression. Seek specialist advice early
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No cause found: under specialist guidance, consider a trial of** empiric paracetamol or NSAIDs · antacid/PPI · laxatives · bisphosphonates if osteopenia is suspected · gabapentin for neuropathic pain · melatonin for sleep.
claims.source_text: Under guidance of specialist, consider trial of medication if unable to identify cause eg Empiric analgesia with paracetamol or NSAIDs Antacid/PPI Laxatives, see constipation Bisphosphonates, if osteopenia suspected Gabapentin, for neuropathic pain Medications for sleep, eg melatonin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider physiotherapy and OT** for positioning, seating and splinting, and **dietetics** for diet or feed type.
claims.source_text: Consider physiotherapy and occupational therapy for positioning, seating, splinting etc Consider dietetics for assessment of diet/feed type
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** when no cause is found and pain persists despite simple analgesia, or analgesic needs escalate beyond simple analgesia.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when No identifiable cause has been found for pain/irritability and ongoing pain/irritability despite adequate simple analgesia Escalating analgesic requirements beyond simple analgesia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the pain or irritability has been assessed and managed, with follow-up arranged.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Pain or irritability has been appropriately assessed and managed and follow up arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - pain and irritability' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_Pain_and_Irritability/, retrieved 2026-09-23
